what_it_does: Photonic chips process data using pulses of light rather than electrical signals, which can be far faster and more energy-efficient for certain AI computations like multiplying large matrices of numbers together. The challenge is that designing such systems requires thinking simultaneously about optics (how light behaves), electronics (the supporting circuits), and the overall chip architecture — but no single simulation tool spans all those levels. SimPhony is a software framework that bridges this gap: it lets designers model a multi-core photonic AI chip, simulate the flow of data through it, and estimate energy use and area, all in one place. It can also connect directly to machine-learning training software, enabling end-to-end evaluation of a photonic AI accelerator from the light-physics level up to model accuracy.
